prep.gitTest: I created my repository by logging into GitHub and clicking on New Repository. I gave my repository a name and created it. after that, I opened my repository in GitHub Codespaces so could work on my files. I used index.html to create and edit my webpage. prep.video1: The video introduces the game development process using Unity. I learned that creating a game involves different steps, including planning, designing, programming, and testing. I want to learn more about how Unity works and how C# is used to make games.
prep.video2: The video explains why having a good mindset is important in game development. I learned developers need to be creative, patient, and willing to learn from their mistakes. It also talks about challenges like technical problems, adding too many features, and burnout. One thing I found useful was setting small goals and staying organized instead of trying to do everything at once, I think this can help me as I continue learning programming.
prep.video3: I learned that organizing your folders and files is important when creating a game because it makes everything easier to find. The video showed how to create a main project folder and use different folders to keep things organized. One thing i found useful was the dolog.txt file because it helps you keep track of your progress. My question is, do we need to create all these folders manually, or can we use a tool to create them automatically.
prep.video4: I learned that documentation is important when creating a game because it helps keep everything organized and makes it easier to understand the project. The video showed how a Game Development can be used to the game's features, goals, and progress. One thing i found useful was using README files to explain what each folder contains. My question is, do we need to create a Game Development Document even if we are working on a small game by ourselves?
prep.video5: I learned how to get started with Unity and how to create a new game project using Unity Hub. The video showed the different parts of the Unity Editor, like the Hierarchy, Scene View, Game View, and Inspector. One thing I found useful was learning how to test a game using the Play button and move the character with WASD. My question is, can I use the Third Person Core template to create my own game instead of starting completely from scratch?
prep.video6: The video shows how to import a custom player into Unity instead of using the default character. I learned that you can customize your game by adding different character models and organizing their files in your project. One thing I found useful was seeing how the character can be changed to make the game more unique. My question is, can I use any 3D character model in Unity, or does it need to be compatible with the game?
prep.opinion: I think this game development pipeline can help me create my own game by showing me how to plan and organize everything before starting. For my project, I want to make a simple 3D game where the player moves around and collects coins. The videos helped me understand how to set up a Unity project, organize files, and customize characters. I think following these steps will make it easier to build my game and fix problems along the way.
prep.questions: Before starting my project, I want to know what the easiest way to create a simple game in Unity is. I also want to know how to organize my files, test my game, and upload everything to GitHub. Since I’m still learning, I want to keep my game simple and focus on making sure it works.

huddle.mission: I chose to create a simple 3D Roll-a-Ball game using Unity. The player will control a ball using the keyboard and move it around a platform. My goal is to make a basic playable game that works correctly.
huddle.framework: I decided to use the ADD/P2P framework to help organize my project. I will start by planning my simple 3D Roll-a-Ball game, then build it step by step in Unity. I will test the ball movement, fix any problems, and make sure the game works before submitting it.

My production plan is to create a simple 3D Roll-a-Ball game in Unity. First, I will create a platform and a sphere. Next, I will add a C# script to control the ball using the keyboard. Finally, I will test the game, fix any errors, and make sure the ball moves correctly. I will complete all tasks myself.
huddle.tech: I decided to use Unity 6 to create my 3D Roll-a-Ball game because it has the tools needed to build a simple 3D game. I will use C# to program the ball’s movement and Visual Studio Code to write and edit my scripts. I will use basic Unity objects like a sphere and a cube for the ball and platform, so I won’t need extra assets or packages. I will also use GitHub to save my project. Since I am working alone, I will check everything myself by testing the game and making sure the controls work correctly.
huddle.reuse: I can reuse the player movement script, camera controls, and basic game objects in future Unity projects. These will help me create other simple 3D games faster. I will use Unity’s built-in tools and my own code. If I use outside assets or code, I will check their licenses and give credit when required.
huddle.boardNotes: I decided to create a simple 3D Roll-a-Ball game using Unity and C#. My plan is to make a ball that moves around a platform using keyboard controls. I will work alone and use GitHub to save my progress. My main question is how to make the movement and camera work correctly. I will test the game in Unity and fix any problems I find. There are no team disagreements because I am working solo.
